newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rainbow Chicken sees continued losses.
newsitem.headline: Rainbow Chicken sees continued losses.

text.p: Struggling poultry producer Rainbow Chicken Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to report a further loss in the six months to September 1997.

"Some benefits of the programme of investment in facilities and people launched in 1996 should start becoming evident in the second half of the year," it added in a statement with results for the year to March 31.
It said significant cost savings had been achieved and more would be realised in the new year.
Rainbow said cash management remained a top priority and capital expenditure was being limited to depreciation flowback and allocated to projects with the highest returns.
Rainbow said its Epol operation had continued to operate effectively. Epol had also competed successfully in the open market in the supply of products to many customers other than Rainbow, it said.
There had been further improvement in the health of the Rainbow flock, it said.
"Over the past year there has been further improvement as measured by declining mortalities."
"The rates of growth of broilers and the efficiency of conversion of feed into meat have improved but are still short of standard," Rainbow said.
The company said risk management had revealed shortcomings in control in several areas of the Rainbow operations and these were being rigorously addressed on a priority basis.
